verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input to this claim is on the public wire and has been for years: the Nov-2021 authorisation is a GlobeNewswire release, the Sep-2022 (effective Nov 2 2022) and Sep-2023 (effective Nov 2 2023) authorisations are filed 6-Ks, and the FY2025 20-F filed 2026-04-29 states in terms that 'on September 3, 2025 the board authorized up to US$10,000 thousand ... over the 12 months starting from September 4, 2025.' The 2026-09-03 release itself is wire copy carried by GlobeNewswire, Nasdaq, Manila Times and StockTitan. So the rollover is assemblable by anyone who opens the last five annual releases. What is not published anywhere I can find is the word 'rollover' — no article, no note, no aggregator drew the line, and the market paid +21.49% on 2,789,500 ADSs (median 20d before: 4,600) for a headline it evidently read as new capital return. That tape is affirmative evidence the conclusion is NOT in the price, which is why this does not sit above 50. Two corrections, though. First, the claim is factually wrong on its own detail: per the FY2025 20-F the prior programme ran 12 months from 2026-09-04's predecessor date of September 4, 2025 — i.e. to 2026-09-04, which is one day AFTER the new programme began on 2026-09-03. There was no four-day gap; there was a one-day overlap. The substantive point survives and is arguably strengthened, but the stated fact is wrong. Second, the mechanism only reaches tonight's print indirectly: the buyback is not in the Q2 release, so this only pays if a soft print becomes the trigger for unwinding a 74% five-day run built on it.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The only usable baseline statement is the tape, and it argues AGAINST the claim being priced: spot 3.42 at 14:07 UTC (quoted $3.96 intraday), +74.5% 5-day, +42.5% 20-day, realised vol 116% annualised, no option chain at all so no implied move and no skew. The single date-matched reaction of +21.49% on 2026-09-03 with 2,789,500 ADSs against a 4,600 pre-event median is the market paying up for the release, not discounting it as a rollover. I am not using the recorded 4.29% median or the 2-of-8 up-count as an earnings base rate — the baseline flags that history as untrustworthy for this FPI.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Any article or note published between 2026-09-03 and tonight's close that identifies the authorisation as a rollover of an expiring identical programme would push this above 70; conversely, evidence that the +21.49% was driven by something other than the buyback release would push it below 20.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every figure checks out exactly against the primary source: the Q1 2026 6-K exhibit shows net revenues RMB99.5m (+359.0%), net loss RMB19.4m, deferred revenue and advances RMB165.9m at 2025-12-31 falling to RMB104.5m at 2026-03-31, and cash+restricted+term deposits RMB407.0m falling to RMB352.4m. So the data is public, it has been public since 2026-06-16, and the market saw it: the stock fell 4.58% that day. That is the case for pricing. The case against is stronger. The datum sits as two unremarked line items on the face of a balance sheet inside a 6-K exhibit; every piece of coverage I can find — GlobeNewswire, StockTitan, GuruFocus, Investing.com's transcript writeup, Simply Wall St — leads on '+359% revenue', 'gross margin 61.9% from 36.2%' and 'loss narrowed 37%', and none of them mentions deferred revenue. Management did not mention deferred revenue, pre-sales, billings or cash burn anywhere on the Q1 call. So the fact is published in an obscure place with its implication drawn nowhere, which is the 20-40 band. Two things hold it off a lower number. The interpretation is contested: prior-year seasonality was a drawdown too (RMB40.4m at 2024-12-31 to RMB36.9m at 2025-03-31, per the Q1 2025 release), so Q1 draws down as a rule — this one is just far bigger. And the sign is not one-way: implied new billings of ~RMB38m against ~RMB18m a year earlier is still more than a doubling, and RMB104.5m of remaining deferred revenue is 2.8x the year-ago balance. 'Drawn largely out of a one-off pre-sale balance rather than new demand' overstates what the numbers show. The cash leg is the harder half: RMB54.6m of cash out against a RMB19.4m accounting loss is real and it is 2.8x, on a company whose entire market capitalisation (~10.84m ADS at 1 ADS : 50 shares, times spot) is below its own cash balance.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The date-matched single reaction to the release that contained this data was -4.58% on 2026-06-17 — the market fell on the print, so it was not read as an unambiguous positive, but 4.58% is nowhere near a full re-rate of a company that has since run +74% in five sessions on unrelated news. No option chain exists, so there is no skew and no implied move to test whether downside is being paid for. Nothing else in the baseline supports or refutes this.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Tonight's Q2 balance sheet showing deferred revenue rebuilt above RMB165.9m would refute the claim outright rather than price it; a published note or article dated before tonight that draws out the drawdown would move it above 60.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is in aggregator wire copy and it moved the stock on the day it became known. TipRanks ran 'Replaces Deloitte With Marcum Asia as Auditor' and StockTitan ran 'Auditor switch at 17 Education (NASDAQ: YQ) from Deloitte to Marcum Asia', both off the 6-K of 2026-05-28, and the stock fell 3.99% that session. A Big Four to small-cap-China-specialist auditor switch at a Chinese ADR is one of the most reflexively flagged governance events there is; it is not obscure and it is not undrawn. Beyond the pricing question, the mechanism to tonight barely exists. The claim's own hook — 'the Q2 2026 numbers about to be released are the first reported under the new firm' — is close to vacuous: these are unaudited quarterly results from a foreign private issuer, Marcum Asia is engaged for the year ending 2026-12-31, and no auditor signs or is named in a 6-K quarterly release. The engagement bites at the FY2026 audit in spring 2027, not tonight. The one thing the claim adds that the wire copy did not is the juxtaposition with the Q1 revenue-recognition inflection, and I will credit that as the reason this is 75 and not 90 — but the 6-K also states plainly that there were no disagreements, no reportable events, and no qualified or modified opinions in 2024 or 2025, which is the disclosure that lets the market file this and move on, and it evidently did.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the same document and substantially the same arithmetic as YQ-a#1, so it inherits the same publication status: the numbers are exact against the 6-K exhibit of 2026-06-17, the market saw that release and fell 4.58%, and no piece of coverage anywhere draws out the deferred revenue line. It is scored a shade higher than a#1 because the extra step it takes is the weaker one. 'Implied new billings of about RMB38m, less than the RMB43.2m spent on sales and marketing' is a rhetorical benchmark, not a threshold that means anything: billings-below-S&M is the normal condition of a consumer product in year one of national launch, and the same computation for Q1 2025 gives implied billings of ~RMB18m against S&M of RMB13m, so the comparison has moved in the company's favour on a growth basis even as it fails the absolute test. The 'so RMB61.4m of the RMB99.5m was a drawdown of Q4 2025 pre-sale orders' framing also assumes the deferred balance runs off one-for-one into revenue with no new deferral inside the quarter, which the disclosure does not support — RMB104.5m of deferred revenue remained, 2.8x the year-ago RMB36.9m. The cash leg is the part I cannot argue with: RMB54.6m out against a RMB19.4m book loss, on a balance sheet whose US$51.1m of cash exceeds the company's entire market capitalisation at ~10.84m ADS-equivalent. That is material, it is unremarked, and tonight's Q2 balance sheet resolves it directly.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The authorisation itself is wire copy from 2026-09-03 and the prior authorisations are filed 6-Ks and press releases, so the 'fourth identical US$10m programme' half is assemblable from public documents and is the weaker version of what YQ-a#0 says. The execution statistic is the genuinely undrawn part — I could not find any article, note or aggregator that states how little has actually been repurchased — but I can partly refute the framing from the same class of document the claim cites. The FY2025 20-F, filed 2026-04-29, discloses repurchases of 105,636,192 Class A shares (2,112,724 ADSs) for RMB51,393 thousand in FY2023 — roughly US$7.2m, i.e. most of a full US$10m programme actually executed. FY2024 was RMB1,070 thousand (~US$0.15m) and FY2025 was RMB3,516 thousand (~US$0.5m). So 'about 1% of the authorisation' is true of the single worst year and is not the company's record; the honest recent number is ~5% of the last programme, and the honest full record includes one programme executed at ~70%. That said, the directional point survives and it matters more here than it would elsewhere: US$10m against a market capitalisation of roughly US$40m is 25% of the company, so if the market is capitalising the authorisation at anything like face value it is capitalising something the issuer spent US$0.5m on over the preceding twelve months. That gap is real and undrawn, which is why this is not above 50.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I checked this against the primary sources and the core factual claim holds up better than most things I judged today. Two of the Form 4s covering the July and August purchases (accessions 0001193125-26-308294 and 0001193125-26-361706) carry aff10b5One = false and no footnote referencing any trading plan, and StockTitan's own summary of the 2026-09-03 Form 4 reads 'CEO purchased 10,284 ADSs without preset plan'. Meanwhile TipRanks ran the conviction framing outright: 'CEO's Bold Move Signals Growing Confidence in EdTech Leader'. So the narrative the claim is attacking is real and published, and the correction genuinely first appears in today's 13D/A. Three things keep this from being a low number. First, the 13D/A is public and an aggregator has already summarised it before the close — StockTitan's YQ overview carries a 2026-09-08 item headed 'An insider stock-buying plan at 17 Education (YQ) runs into 2028'. It is hours old and obscure, but it is out, and the stock is up ~4% today with it out. Second, the claim mislocates it: the plan is disclosed in Item 3 of the 13D/A, not Item 6, and Item 6 in fact says there are no other contracts or arrangements. Third and most important, the size does not support the rhetoric. The 13D/A states Future Glory bought 110,628 ADSs (5,531,400 Class A shares) for approximately US$0.24 million between 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-03. Debunking a US$240,000 signal on a company with roughly US$40m of market capitalisation is a sentiment correction, not a numbers event, and it does not touch tonight's P&L at all.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves of this are separately published and one of them moved the stock on the day. The auditor switch was carried by TipRanks and StockTitan on 2026-05-28 and the shares fell 3.99% that session. The Marcum Asia sanction is a PCAOB press release of 2025-09-23 and was covered by Accounting Today, CPA Practice Advisor and International Accounting Bulletin the following day; the numbers in the claim — censure, US$100,000 civil penalty — are exactly right. So there is no unpublished fact here, only an unpublished juxtaposition, and I score it marginally below the sibling YQ-a#2 only because the PCAOB detail has never been attached to YQ specifically. The juxtaposition is also weaker than it reads. The PCAOB order concerns MarcumBP's transfer of draft workpapers to a successor auditor on Gridsum Holding — a predecessor/successor communications failure on an unrelated issuer, penalised at US$100,000, not an audit-quality finding on a China client's revenue recognition. And the timing hook cuts both ways: the 6-K states there were no disagreements, no reportable events, and no qualified or modified opinions from Deloitte for 2024 or 2025, which is precisely the disclosure that lets a market file an auditor switch and move on. The dates check out — 20-F filed 2026-04-29, dismissal effective 2026-05-27, four weeks — but a four-week gap after a clean 20-F sign-off is also the ordinary time at which an issuer switches auditors, because that is when the prior engagement ends.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the highest number I am giving and it is the one I am most confident in, for three separate reasons. First, it has already been published in exactly this framing on the day of the print: StockTitan's YQ overview carries a 2026-09-08 item headed 'An insider stock-buying plan at 17 Education (YQ) runs into 2028' — the bullish read of the 13D/A is not a discovery, it is today's aggregator headline. Second, the tiny non-insider base is the single most structural and most visible fact about this security. The arithmetic is right (542.2m less 223.9m is 318.3m Class A-equivalent, and at the 1 ADS : 50 ratio effective December 2023 that is 6.37m ADSs) but a small float is not news, it is the permanent condition of the name, and the squeeze it enables is not pending — it has already happened. The stock traded 2,789,500 ADSs on 2026-09-03, roughly 44% of the entire non-Liu base in one session, ran +74.5% in five sessions, and average 20-day volume now stands at 157,802 against the 4,600 the claim cites as the pre-spike median. Citing the 4,600 as if it still described the market is citing a number the run-up already destroyed. Third, the two legs of the 'structural bid' do not survive sizing. The 10b5-1 plan bought 110,628 ADSs for approximately US$0.24 million over nine weeks — about US$27,000 a week — against current dollar volume of several hundred thousand a day; that is not a bid, it is a rounding error, and the 13D/A explicitly says the plan is subject to price restrictions and volume limitations while every disclosed execution fell between roughly US$1.89 and US$2.46, well below the current US$3.96. There is no evidence in the document that the plan buys anything at all up here, which would invert the claim outright. The US$10m authorisation leg is refuted by the hunters' own other finding: the FY2025 20-F shows US$0.5m actually repurchased over the last twelve months, so a live authorisation is not a live bid.

Spot 3.42 at the baseline snapshot (quoted $3.96 intraday), +74.5% over five sessions, +42.5% over twenty, realised vol 116% annualised, 20-day average volume 157,802 against the 4,600 pre-spike median the claim relies on, and 2,789,500 ADSs printed on 2026-09-03. A structural squeeze that has already delivered +74% and a 34x volume expansion is expressed in the price, not waiting in it. No option chain, so nothing to say about skew.

interactions:
Three pairs rest on one document each, and one pair is two opposite-signed readings of the same document.

SAME DOCUMENT, near-duplicate: YQ-a#1 and YQ-b#0 both rest entirely on the Q1 2026 6-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821468/000119312526273326/yq-ex99_1.htm, filed 2026-06-17). Identical figures, identical mechanism; b#0 adds only the billings-vs-S&M comparison and the same cash number to one more decimal. They should not be counted as two independent findings — they are one finding found twice, and I have priced them within two points of each other deliberately.

SAME UNDERLYING FACT, two filings: YQ-a#0 and YQ-b#1 are both the 2026-09-03 buyback release read as an empty rollover. a#0 enumerates six authorisations and gets the expiry wrong (the prior programme ran to 2026-09-04, one day AFTER the new one started on 2026-09-03, per the FY2025 20-F — there was an overlap, not a four-day gap); b#1 enumerates a more conservative four and adds the execution statistic from the FY2024 20-F. b#1's execution figure is the only genuinely undrawn datum across the pair, and it is itself partly refuted by the FY2025 20-F, which shows RMB51.4m (~US$7.2m) actually repurchased in FY2023.

SAME DOCUMENT, one adds a detail: YQ-a#2 and YQ-b#3 both rest on the auditor-change 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526243134/yq-6k-05-26-2026.htm, 2026-05-28). b#3 adds the PCAOB censure of Marcum Asia; a#2 adds the 'first quarter under the new firm' hook, which is close to vacuous because Marcum is engaged for the FY2026 audit and does not sign unaudited quarterly 6-K results. Again one event, found twice.

DIRECT CONTRADICTION, one document: YQ-b#2 and YQ-b#4 are opposite-signed readings of the SAME Schedule 13D/A filed this morning (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1821468/000119312526384376/primary_doc.xml). b#2 reads the 10b5-1 plan as evidence the CEO buying is mechanical and therefore not a signal (bearish); b#4 reads the same plan running to 2028 as a structural bid under the stock (bullish). They cannot both be worth much, and on the document's own numbers neither is: the plan bought US$0.24m over nine weeks under price and volume restrictions, at executions between roughly US$1.89 and US$2.46 against a US$3.96 spot. That sizing simultaneously caps b#2's debunking value and destroys b#4's bid.

SECOND CONTRADICTION, across hunters: YQ-b#4's second leg — 'the US$10m authorisation is live' as a source of support — is refuted by YQ-a#0 and YQ-b#1, which show the same authorisation is a rollover the issuer has spent US$0.5m against in the last twelve months. One hunter's bullish structural bid is the other hunter's empty rollover, and it is the same US$10m.

Finally, a defect running across a#0, b#1 and b#4: all three lean on the pre-spike 4,600-ADS median daily volume, whether as a squeeze setup or as the backdrop to the +21.49% move. Average 20-day volume is now 157,802 and 2,789,500 ADSs printed on 2026-09-03. Any argument built on 4,600 is built on a number the run-up has already invalidated.
